discovery: Prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulators

nominees.name: Qi-Kun Xue
nominees.affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology and Tsinghua University, China

nominees.name: Zhong Fang
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, China

nominees.name: Xi Dai
nominees.affiliation: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, China

motivation: The quantum anomalous Hall effect, quantized Hall conductance without any external magnetic field, was proposed by Haldane in 1988 but long considered unrealizable. In 2010 Fang and Dai, with collaborators, identified a concrete route: magnetically doped Bi2Se3-family thin films, where exchange-induced band inversion yields a Chern insulator. In 2013 Xue's team, after years of perfecting molecular-beam epitaxy of Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 films with atomic-level control of thickness, doping and charge neutrality, observed the Hall resistance quantized at h/e^2 at zero field with near-vanishing longitudinal resistance. This is a true '0 to 1' discovery: a new quantum state of matter, the first topological phase realized with intrinsic magnetism, and dissipationless chiral edge transport. It opened the fields of magnetic topological materials (MnBi2Te4), axion insulators and proposed topological quantum devices and resistance standards, and has been reproduced worldwide.
